title: PlayStation Joins the Family Guard Dashboard | vitalii.no
description:
The router only sees a PlayStation as one more address on the Wi-Fi table — it has no idea which child is signed in, whether they're actually playing a game or just idling on the home screen, or what title is running. Managing PlayStation time meant walking into the room and looking at the screen.

I added agent/psn.py, which authenticates against the PlayStation Network using the parent account's own token and reads presence for every family member linked to that account — online status, current title, and whether it's an actual game session or just the dashboard. That feed merges into the same device table the Wi-Fi and Android TV agents already populate, so a PlayStation session shows up next to every other screen in the house.

The guard dashboard now shows, per child, whether they're on PlayStation right now and what they're playing, using the same daily-limit and block logic that already covers Wi-Fi devices and the TV stick. The result: zero walks down the hall just to check.
